_comment: OBSERVED SPECIMEN — not constructed. Do not 'tidy' this file.
Microsoft Teams transcript, exported from the meeting chat as .docx and
captured 15 Aug 2026 from a business-tier tenant (the same call whose
filename grammar is pinned in tests/test_ingest.py).
THE POINT OF THIS FILE IS THE EMBEDDED NEWLINES. Teams packs an entire
turn — the 'Name  0:04' header AND every line of speech under it — into
ONE paragraph, separated by <w:br/>, which python-docx returns as '\n'
inside paragraph.text. Paragraph 3 below carries 8 of them.
A parser that treats a paragraph as a line therefore sees one unmatched
blob per turn, matches no speaker header, and falls through to the
untimed path: 5 segments, every one at start_time=0.0 with no speaker.
That is what this real file did while the constructed one-line-per-
paragraph tests alongside it passed — the same failure shape as
_TEAMS_SUFFIX_RE and Swift's TeamsRecordingName, recorded in
docs/design-cloud-import.md §6.
No redaction was applied. The speaker name is the capturing user's own
and is already public as the repo's git author; the long Microsoft
privacy-policy passage is boilerplate the participant read aloud.
KNOWN RESIDUE, deliberately left visible: Teams brackets a transcript
with '<Name> started transcription' / '<Name> stopped transcription'.
The opening marker precedes the first header and is dropped; the closing
one trails the final turn and is currently appended to it as speech.
Stripping it needs either the English literal (localisation-fragile, the
trap this module avoids) or a rule that risks eating a genuine last line
beginning with the speaker's name. Deferred pending a multi-turn
specimen to design against.
